title: ORLIS: Obfuscation-Resilient Library Detection for Android
venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Mobile Software Engineering and Systems (MOBILESoft)
detection_method: Two-stage approach: (1) coarse sdhash app-level filtering to narrow candidate libraries; (2) fine-grained ssdeep CFG hashing + Jaccard similarity for class-level matching
module_decoupling: None explicit — operates on decompiled app classes matched against library class profiles; no separate module decoupling phase
features_used: sdhash (context-triggered piecewise hash) for app-level filtering
ssdeep (fuzzy hash) of CFG structures for class-level matching
Jaccard similarity coefficient for partial class matches
matching_algorithm: Two-stage: Stage 1 computes sdhash of full app to filter candidate libraries; Stage 2 computes ssdeep CFG hashes per class and compares via Jaccard similarity against library class profiles
obfuscation_handling: Uses structural CFG features that survive identifier renaming, package flattening, and control-flow modifications; ssdeep fuzzy hashing tolerates minor structural variations
r8_resilience: Not tested (pre-R8 era; tested on Allatori and ProGuard obfuscation)
version_level_f1: Not reported — no version-level detection metrics
recall: Not explicitly reported (F1 of ~62-67% with ~90% precision implies recall of ~48-53%)
speed: ~1,438s per app (slowest among all evaluated tools)
dataset_size: Not explicitly quantified in available data; evaluated on obfuscated apps with Allatori and ProGuard
partial_lib_handling: Yes — Jaccard similarity naturally handles partial library inclusion via set-based overlap scoring
open_source: Not confirmed publicly available; requires Soot environment (difficult installation)
transitive_deps: No — does not handle transitive dependencies
strengths: Pioneered CFG-based matching for obfuscation resilience
~90% precision against Allatori and ProGuard obfuscation
Jaccard similarity provides natural partial library inclusion handling
Two-stage architecture (fast filter + deep check) is a reusable design pattern
Structural CFG features survive renaming, package flattening, and control-flow modifications
weaknesses: Extremely slow (~1,438s/app) — prohibitive for large-scale analysis
Lowest library-level F1 among Gen-1 tools (~62-67%)
impact_on_project: ORLIS demonstrates that CFG-based structural matching is viable for obfuscation resilience but the speed cost is prohibitive. The two-stage architecture (sdhash coarse filter + ssdeep fine match) is a useful design pattern that could be adapted with more efficient hashing. Jaccard similarity for partial library inclusion is a technique worth adopting. However, the ~1,438s/app processing time means ORLIS itself is not usable for production SBOM extraction — any adopted approach must be orders of magnitude faster. The 62-67% F1 also sets a low bar that must be exceeded.
